value: A write that would remove or overwrite an entry it does not name is refused (#216, #224, v1.4.0): a value to a parent of entries, a key under a leaf, or a key differing only by case from an existing one. Covers set, copy, rename, `data import --merge` and the MCP tools; error code INVALID_INPUT; no flag gets past it (-f only skips the overwrite prompt for the same key). Keys compare case-insensitively on every filesystem, so a case-only rename needs a temporary key. The comparison is FLAT over every stored key (utils/keyCollision.ts, no store imports): a walk down the tree follows one branch per segment and misses `A.x` vs `a.x` when a store holds both casings of a branch — the first version did that and an independent review caught it. directoryStore.setOne returns false on any collision and storage.setValue's slow path is what refuses, so a new single-key write path must call assertKeyWritable itself. rename also refuses a destination under its own source or an invalid key: it writes the new keys, then removes the old key with everything under it. Full saves (saveData) are not checked: import replace, remove and rename restructure legitimately. A merge import merges into the one store it writes to; it used to merge into the project-over-global view and copy the global store into the project. Gaps: lint sees a case pair only where both files exist (a case-insensitive checkout would need git's index, and src spawns no git); and a store where a leaf and a key under it are BOTH on disk — which a git merge of two branches can leave, each write having been legal on its own branch — loads as one of the two, and the next full save deletes the other with no warning (lint passes). That one is older than #224 and unfixed. 1.3.0 does all of the removals silently and reports success.
